about.title: Aliso Viejo Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision upends everything, and the practical questions—funeral costs, lost income, what happens next—often arrive before the grief even settles. Aliso Viejo's busiest corridors, including Aliso Creek Road, Pacific Park Drive, Aliso Viejo Parkway, and Alicia Parkway, see a steady flow of traffic each week, with reported collisions clustering on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. While the most recent full year on record shows 73 injury collisions and 103 people injured with zero recorded traffic deaths, fatal crashes can still occur on any Orange County roadway, and families are left to navigate a civil claim separate from any criminal proceeding. Our team handles wrongful death claims and can evaluate the claim, explain California's rules on standing and deadlines, and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. We can help clarify where your family fits before any claim moves forward.

items.title: A Ticking Two-Year Clock
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Getting in touch with us early helps protect that deadline.

items.title: No Upfront Cost While You Grieve
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery. That means you can focus on your family instead of legal bills while the claim is being evaluated.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring the claim. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing instead. We can review your family's specific situation and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Aliso Viejo?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, such as a city or county vehicle on Aliso Viejo Parkway or another local corridor, the deadline to act can be much shorter. It's best to have an attorney review the timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: What losses can a wrongful death claim recover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the family has lost. This is a civil claim, separate from any criminal charges the driver might face. Our team can walk you through how these categories might apply to your case.
